description: Depths of the past month's M2.5+ earthquakes from the USGS feed: a strongly skewed population (most are shallow, a few are hundreds of kilometres deep). Statistics idea: the central limit theorem. 500 random samples of n = 1, 5, 30 and 100 quakes are drawn (with replacement, by a deterministic pseudo-random generator in Polars), and their standardised means approach the normal curve while their spread shrinks as σ/√n and their skewness as γ/√n. Caveats: the population is this month's feed, not all quakes (it over-represents well-monitored networks), and aftershock clusters make the quakes themselves dependent; resampling makes the draws independent.
name: Central limit theorem: earthquake depths
